entities.name: PMID:25096451
observations: Matched comparison of 36 male and 72 female ERAO patients found similar postoperative HHS (94.1 vs 93.5) and no significant sex difference in clinical outcome or survivorship; survival was 92.8% in men versus 98.1% in women after more than 5 years.
Men tended to have smaller CE-angle correction, but the difference was not associated with a significant clinical outcome difference.

entities.name: PMID:17308472
observations: In 273 hips from 248 ERAO patients followed at least 5 years, sex was not an independent predictor of osteoarthritis progression after adjustment for BMI, valgus osteotomy, operative era, postoperative CE angle, and femoral-head position.
Nine hips converted to THA; no sex-specific THA estimate was reported.

entities.name: PMID:21290153
observations: In 340 hips, pubic or ischial stress fractures occurred in 10 hips and all were in women, but multivariable analysis identified pubic discontinuity—not sex—as the independent predictor; fractures united without worse final clinical outcomes.

entities.name: PMID:41371542
observations: A CT-based virtual ERAO study found lower simulated flexion and internal-rotation thresholds in males than females, associated with lower femoral-neck anteversion; this was exploratory and did not measure actual postoperative clinical outcomes.

entities.name: ERAO sex outcomes
observations: Available clinical ERAO evidence does not establish sex as an independent determinant of postoperative HHS, radiographic correction, osteoarthritis progression, complications, or THA-free survivorship.
Evidence is limited because ERAO cohorts are overwhelmingly female and some studies match or adjust for sex rather than being powered to test it.
